newsitem.title: UK: LME ends Tuesday on a volatile note.
newsitem.headline: LME ends Tuesday on a volatile note.

text.p: Traders attention continued to eye the fortunes of the London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc three months delivery price during brisk and volatile trading on Tuesday.
By the close of the LME kerb traders pondered the next direction in a market that has generated wide price gyrations during trading on Tuesday in both forward and spread trading.
Zinc was thrown into a frenzy after an expected rush towards an upside target of $1,700 a tonne failed in early trading. This prompted investment fund selling which plunged prices to a low of $1,370.
A slowing in the pace of declines in LME stocks and whippy nearby backwardations added pressure.
At the close of LME afternoon kerb trading zinc stood at $1,480, well down on Monday's seven year high of $1,674 and close of $1,671.
"General selling amid concern that the market was running far above itself prompted liquidation from all quarters," one zinc trader said.
He believed that further extreme moves will be seen during Wednesday's trading. "Take a pick on where the market is going is the best thing anyone can do at the moment.
During the past month zinc has built up a belief that the market is fundamentally robust despite the slow summer period.
"As far as I am concerned stocks hold the key to the market," another trader said.

Traders continued to digest talk that a deal has been struck between Chinese short position holders and a European merchant. Others suggested the short Chinese smelters were near square after buying forward late Monday and earlier on Tuesday.
But nearby backwardations remained firm which suggested to some that no deal has been struck between the shorts and longs.
Earlier one LME floor trader said that any signs of a conclusion to the settlement of two sides of the market would have seen the nearby dates move swiftly towards contango.
By the close of business zinc's cash to threes settled near $70 after approaching $100 on Monday.

LME stocks fell by 825 tonnes, a cause of concern to several traders after a long string of more sizeable declines. Traders awaited Wednesday's LME stocks returns for confirmeation of a possible change oftrend.
Elsewhere, late afternoon business saw nickel streak ahead as it broke above expected resistance which in turn sparked buy-stops and speculative interest.

Traders said nickel's bounce largely reflected a knee-jerk reaction to an oversold condition. Background support was found from a contract dispute between workers and producer Falconbridge at its Sudbury, Ontario, operations.
Last business was at $7,495, up on $7,290.
Copper moved higher after being earlier depressed by another LME stocks rise. It was last at $2,359, against $2,353. Traders were expecting a period of consolidation on Wednesday.
Aluminium again tested resistance above $1,700 on the back of consumer interest and forward buying. It was last at $1,704, up on $1,674.
Lead was quiet and last at $635, down $2, while tin settled at $5,410, up $10. Alloy was quoted at $1,515/20, little moved.
